title: Risk–control alignment
prompt:
For every RACM row, determine whether the control actually addresses the associated risk.

Assess alignment as one of: Strong, Partial, Weak, Misaligned, No Control.

- Strong: Control directly prevents or detects the stated risk.
- Partial: Control addresses only part of the risk.
- Weak: Control has some relationship but does not adequately mitigate the risk.
- Misaligned: Control does not address the stated risk.
- No Control: Risk exists but no meaningful control is identified.

Also consider: one control mapped to too many unrelated risks; one risk needing multiple controls but only one weak control; control addressing a downstream consequence instead of the root risk; control operating after the risk has already materialized; control dependent on another missing control; risk and control essentially duplicates.

Return alignment, alignment_rationale (max 3 sentences), and proposed_solution (max 3 sentences).
